steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Command words tell you exactly what the examiner wants — misreading them loses marks

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Describe means give a factual account of what you see, hear or know about the dance

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Explain means give reasons — why something happens or why a choreographer made a choice

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Analyse means break down and examine in detail, showing how parts create meaning or effect

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between 'describe' and 'explain' in an AQA 8236 exam? | Q: How should you approach a 'compare' question? | Q: What does 'analyse' require you to do in a dance exam?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 'Describe' requires a factual account of what you observe — what happens in the dance. 'Explain' requires you to give reasons — why it happens or why the choreographer made that choice. Explain includ | Identify both similarities and differences between the two items. Use linking words such as 'similarly' and 'in contrast'. Ensure you address both sides equally and support each point with specific ev | Break the dance or element into its component parts and examine how each part contributes to the overall effect. Show how movement, dynamics, space and relationships work together to create meaning.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Circle or underline the command word before writing anything — it sets your answer direction For 'describe' questions, use specific dance terminology rather than vague descriptions For 'explain' questions, always include the word 'because' to ensure you give reasons In 'compare' questions, avoid writing about one thing then the other separately — link them For 'evaluate' questions, end with a clear judgement statement supported by your evidence
